newsitem.title: NIGERIA: New head needed for giant Nigerian gas project.
newsitem.headline: New head needed for giant Nigerian gas project.

text.p: A new chief executive is to be appointed for Nigerian Liquefied Natural Gas (NLNG), the company handling a $4 billion project to liquefy and export Nigerian gas, industry sources said on Thursday.
The newcomer will succeed Theo Oerlemans, the Dutchman who has held the job for three years.
"After three years Mr Oerlemans is returning to London to a new challenge at Shell International," said one source, adding that "It is a normal career move."
Shell Gas BV is the technical leader in the LNG joint venture with state oil firm Nigerian National Petroleum Corp. The other partners are Elf Aquitaine and Italy's Agip SpA.

A Nigerian newspaper reported on Thursday that Oerlemans' impending return was a new crisis for the project after Italian state power firm Enel -- intended to have been the gas project's chief customer -- cancelled their contract in December.
But NLNG sources dismissed this, saying Oerlemans' move was "a normal rotation in international jobs."
They said Shell's nomination of a replacement for the post was in line with its position as the technical leader in the project, and would have to be approved by the board of directors in Lagos.
"Shell will be issuing in statement from London within the next few days," said one.
Despite Enel's cancellation of its purchase contract, the project is still going ahead in Bonny in Nigeria's southeastern oil-producing region.
The project aims to produce 7.2 billion cubic metres of LNG per year from a plant projected to come on stream in 1999.
Long-term supply contracts have been signed with Enargas of Spain and Gaz de France.

The project came under threat last year when international lobby groups piled pressure on the partners to abandon it over Nigeria's hanging of nine minority rights activists including author Ken Saro-Wiwa for murder.
